commands.notes: Activates a prepared package locally without conflating package activation with canonical phone/tablet item start.
Watch starts or resumes local package audio only after the local audio runtime confirms playback has begun.
Watch pauses local package audio and preserves source media time.
Local skip should resolve through the package timeline, not through text chunk ids or tethered phone state.
Local skip should resolve through the package timeline and remain idempotent at package boundaries.
Watch jumps to the packaged chapter startMs and recomputes transcript segment context locally.
Watch pauses local package playback, captures source media time and transcript segment from the package timeline, and records locally.
Watch saves audio locally and queues an interjection_recorded sync event. Phone/tablet later imports it idempotently.
Watch discards local unsaved recording and resumes package playback from the rollback policy.
Watch untethered has no AI capability. Summary is phone/tablet work after sync import and transcription.
Watch untethered has no discussion capability. Follow-up should occur on phone/tablet after sync import.
Watch may queue a session_finished event, but canonical session completion is reconciled by phone/tablet.

backendRequests.title: Add package-specific loadWatchPackage command
backendRequests.details: Command matrix and SessionKit expose loadWatchPackage for prepared package activation.

backendRequests.title: Add idempotent importWatchSyncEvent command
backendRequests.details: Command matrix and SessionKit expose importWatchSyncEvent. Phone/tablet imports each watch event once by event id, preserving audio and anchors before transcription.

backendRequests.title: Build shared media timeline anchor resolver
backendRequests.details: SessionKit now exposes MediaTimelineAnchorResolver for source media time, transcript segment, chapter, playback-rate observation, and optional text range anchoring.

backendRequests.title: Publish package availability and transfer statuses
backendRequests.details: Phone publishes package availability rows and Watch merges them with local manifests to distinguish loaded, queued for transfer, pre-rendered but not loaded, not yet pre-rendered, rendering, failed, and expired package states.

backendRequests.title: Add durable package request event
backendRequests.details: Watch taps send durable package request events. Phone persists prerender_requested and watch_transfer_requested, and starts package transfer for available packages.

backendRequests.title: Define multi-device iCloud package manifest
backendRequests.details: Laptop, phone, and tablet should be able to share package manifests and assets through a user-owned sync container. Watch should still receive assets through an explicit phone-mediated transfer path.

backendRequests.title: Implement local Watch audio playback with source time
backendRequests.details: SessionKitAudio exposes PreparedAudioPlaybackClient with current media time and completion state. Watch untethered uses it through a local SessionEngine when package audio assets are present.

backendRequests.title: Define reconnect merge and conflict policy
backendRequests.details: Watch sync events are sent durably and imported through SessionEngine.importWatchSyncEvent, which is idempotent by event id. Interjection imports create anchored records without being overwritten by playback-position events.

notes: Gate 4 starts from watch-untethered, not watch-tethered plus more delegated commands.
Pre-rendered TTS packages and first-party audio/podcast sessions should share the same transcript/media timeline anchoring model once either has timestamped transcript segments.
The Watch owns package playback and recording locally, but not transcription, cleanup, summary, discussion, provider calls, canonical persistence, or package rendering.

The companion reconnect trace uses phone-tablet-online and should be owned by the steward or a phone-import gate contract because surface contract validation requires trace runtimeProfile to match the surface runtimeProfile.
Package request and transfer status probably require new snapshot fields or a separate package library model; those shared contract changes are steward-owned.
